answer: Sequential compute-quota identity. Each identity is minted only after its agent completes a verifiable compute task whose output depends on the prior identity's state, forming a chain like a comet's tail that cannot be parallelized. Registration is free but serialized: an attacker must run the full chain, so N identities cost N sequential compute-hours, not one bulk payment. A harbor rule caps chain branching per epoch, and an oasis checkpoint every 1,000 links forces revalidation. Attacker cost scales linearly in wall-clock compute, not capital.
